newsitem.title: USA: Farley's "Ninja" packs punch at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Farley's "Ninja" packs punch at U.S. box office.

text.p: A bumbling martial arts expert overpowered a wise-cracking San Francisco cop at the weekend box office as "Beverly Hills Ninja" opened in the top spot, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

"Beverly Hills Ninja," a comedy starring Chris Farley, earned an estimated $10 million during the Friday to Sunday period, while Eddie Murphy's "Metro" opened in second with about $9.3 million. Final data will be released on Monday.
The big-screen version of "Evita," starring Madonna and Jonathan Pryce, slipped a notch to third with $7.2 million.
Last week's number one, "The Relic," slid to fifth with $6.7 million, narrowly behind "Jerry Maguire" with $6.8 million.

"Beverly Hills Ninja" features Farley as an out-of-shape martial arts hero raised by Ninjas in Japan. It was released by Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures unit, and averaged a creditable $4,970 from 2,112 screens.

In "Metro," Murphy plays a San Francisco hostage negotiator in a role that recalls his three "Beverly Hills Cop" movies. Released by Walt Disney Co.'s Touchstone Pictures banner, it averaged $4,648 from 2001 screens.

"Evita" earned $7.2 million at the weekend after expanding its screen count to 923 from 704. Its $7,801 screen average was the highest in the top 10. Since opening Christmas Day in the United States on two screens, it has earned $21.4 million.
Disney distributes "Evita" in the United States, while Sony handles "Jerry Maguire." "The Relic" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..
